details.description: GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's (Zhipu AI) current flagship large language model, released August 18, 2026, built for complex software engineering, long-horizon agentic tasks and cybersecurity vulnerability research. It uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with Dynamic Sparse Activation, supports a 1,048,576-token context window with up to 128,000 tokens of output, and always reasons at a configurable low, high or max effort level. Z.ai reports a 50% improvement over GLM-5.2 on its internal Code Bench, and Fireworks AI recommends it as the migration target for GLM-5.2 users.
advantages: Z.ai reports a 50% performance gain over GLM-5.2 on Z.ai's internal Code Bench, calling GLM-5.3 the most capable open-weights coding model (Z.ai docs / Hugging Face model card).
Scores 78.1 on the FrontierSWE benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 84.5 on CyberGym, a cybersecurity vulnerability-discovery benchmark, per its Hugging Face model card.
Supports three configurable reasoning effort levels (low, high, max) for coding and agentic tasks (Z.ai docs).
disadvantages: Text-only input and output, with no image, audio or video support (Fireworks AI, Z.ai docs).
Documented language support is limited to English and Chinese (Hugging Face model card).
use_cases: Complex software engineering and long-horizon coding-agent workflows
Cybersecurity vulnerability discovery and exploit research

notes: Z.ai's own GitHub repository (zai-org/GLM-5) lists GLM-5.3 at 744B-A40B parameters, close to the 743B figure on Fireworks' hosted model page, while Z.ai's Hugging Face model card instead states 'Model size: 753B params'; docs.z.ai's own guide page does not give a parameter count at all. Since maker-controlled sources disagree, parameter count is left out of the description. Catalog's max_output_tokens (128000) and max_input_tokens (1048576) match both Fireworks' and Z.ai's stated figures.
